judge_assessment.explanation: Every positive judge claim checks out against the artifacts. I recomputed all six machine items independently: midpoint of A(-6,2)/B(4,8) = (-1,5); PR from (0,0) to (3,4) = 5 with QR = 5 and PQ = 6, so the triangle is isosceles and not equilateral; slope of CM = (3-(-2))/(-1-3) = -5/4 against AB's 2/3, product -5/6 which is not -1; QR = 3 for the 6-by-3 rectangle; slope of CD = -3/4 against AB's 4/3 with both segments of length 5; and (3/4)(m/3) = -1 gives m = -4. The two manual items are genuinely manual and genuinely correct: problem 7's WXYZ has perpendicular diagonals (WY vertical, XZ horizontal) with sides 5, sqrt45, sqrt45, 5, so it satisfies the loose statement and is a kite; problem 8's model isosceles trapezoid A(0,0) B(6,0) C(5,3) D(1,3) has AC = BD = sqrt34 with a non-right angle at A. Where I part company is the perfect instruction_following score. The task contract asks for HSG-CO.A / HSG-CO.C and final_response.md states that "those codes do not appear in this skill's references/standards-map.md" - that statement is false; the map lists "Congruence: transformations, triangle congruence, proofs | HSG-CO.A-HSG-CO.D" at line 111. The judge also did not test the prompt's "clearly label any genuinely open response" clause against problems 1-5, each of which prints a required written explanation that no verify entry records.

strengths_to_preserve: The directions table binds each verbal definition to a computable coordinate test (midpoint to the averaging formula, congruent to the distance formula, perpendicular to m1*m2 = -1). That single decision is what turns 'find a counterexample' into arithmetic instead of argument, and all eight problems then sit on that footing.

Problem 7's quadrilateral W(0,0) X(3,4) Y(0,10) Z(-3,4) is a precisely chosen kite: the diagonals really are perpendicular so the loose 'definition' is satisfied, while the side lengths 5, sqrt45, sqrt45, 5 kill it. Part (c) - 'the student's statement is still true of every rhombus; what is it, if not a definition?' - is the item that teaches the property/definition distinction, and the key answers it with the biconditional idea rather than a label.

The manual answers carry accept/reject criteria, not just model text. Problem 8's key requires (i) specific vertices, (ii) both diagonal lengths shown equal, (iii) the named failing condition, and explicitly rejects 'a trapezoid' with no coordinates. That is what makes a manual flag a grading instrument rather than an abdication.
The study guide's watch-out box states the distinction the whole sheet turns on in two sentences: "'Not a definition' does not mean 'false'. Every rhombus really does have perpendicular diagonals."

root_causes.description: SKILL.md tells the author to take standards codes from references/standards-map.md and never to invent one, but it never says to SEARCH that file for the standard the request actually names. The result is a silent nearest-neighbour substitution plus a delivered claim that the map lacks the code - and the map's header explicitly warns against exactly this ("say so rather than reaching for the nearest one"). No gate inspects the tag, so the substitution passes every check.
evidence: final_response.md: "The task references HSG-CO.A / HSG-CO.C, but those codes do not appear in this skill's references/standards-map.md, and the skill forbids inventing codes."
references/standards-map.md line 111: "| Congruence: transformations, triangle congruence, proofs | HSG-CO.A-HSG-CO.D |" - the row exists and covers HSG-CO.C.
verify.json tags all eight problems "HSG-GPE.B.4-B.7", so the answer key's Curriculum block prints coordinate-geometry-proof codes for a definitions-and-proof-logic sheet.

root_causes.description: Hybrid items - compute a value, then justify what it proves - are recorded with only their computational entry. The written half is a printed response slot that no verify entry covers and that the gate log never reports, so the build's '6 machine-verified, 2 manual' summary understates how much of the sheet needs a human.
evidence: Worksheet problem 4 prints three enumerated slots - (a) write its converse, (b) compute QR, (c) explain why PQRS makes the converse false - under a single 'Answer:' line; verify.json id 4 is one distance entry expecting 3.

Problems 1, 2, 3 and 5 each end with a required sentence ('state in one sentence why the student's wording fails', 'say which wording decides', 'Explain what your answer proves about Kai's statement', 'explain in one sentence why these two segments form a counterexample'); none has a manual entry.
gate_log.txt step 5 reports '6 passed - 0 failed - 2 manual', counting only problems 7 and 8.

improvements.title: Search references/standards-map.md for the requested code family before substituting a different standard, and never assert the map lacks a code without searching
improvements.proposed_change: Two changes. (1) SKILL.md's tagging paragraph currently says only "a code from references/standards-map.md - never invent codes". Add the missing first step: before writing any "standard" value, do a literal substring search of references/standards-map.md for the code family the request names (HSG-CO, HSG-GMD, HSG-MG, HSN-CN, HSN-RN, HSA-REI.A, ...) and for the topic words, and use the matching row's code. Only when that search genuinely returns nothing may the sheet deviate, and the map's own header rule then applies verbatim: "say so rather than reaching for the nearest one", plus add the real row in the same change. Forbid stating in final_response.md that a code is absent from the map unless that search was actually run. (2) Add a band-consistency lint to scripts/verify.py: compare each problem's "standard" prefix with the course level the answer key declares and fail the build when a High-School sheet is tagged with a K-8 code (8.G, 7.EE, 6.EE, ...), printing the high-school rows of the map as the alternatives.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture tests/fixtures/standards_band_mismatch/: a verify JSON whose ten problems are all tagged "8.G.C.9", paired with an answer key whose declared level is "High School Geometry - Modeling with Measurement". scripts/verify.py must exit non-zero and name HSG-GMD.A.1-A.3 / HSG-MG.A.1-A.3 from the map. Run against the current tree the fixture passes silently, which is exactly how curr-345 shipped with a fully green gate chain.
improvements.expected_impact: Removes a demonstrably false statement about the repository's own reference file from delivered responses, and puts the contracted standard back on the answer key's Curriculum block - the one line a parent or teacher reads to place the sheet in a course. Six of the ten cases in this shard are affected.
improvements.risk: Low. The lint is additive and fires only on a grade-prefix/course mismatch. The care point is band vocabulary: an Algebra 2 or Pre-Algebra sheet can legitimately carry an 8.EE-style code for review material, so the lint should warn rather than fail when the course string is a middle-school or transitional course.

improvements.title: One verify entry per printed response slot, including enumerated sub-parts and trailing second questions
improvements.proposed_change: Require the verify JSON to carry as many entries under an id as the printed problem has response slots. Sub-parts written as (a)/(b)/(c), and trailing extra questions ('Then check: what is m<A?', 'State how many zeros the theorem supplied'), each need their own entry - machine-typed where a value is computable, manual where it is not. Add a lint that, per problem segment of the worksheet .tex, counts enumerated \item sub-parts and \ansline / \answerline occurrences and fails when that count exceeds the number of verify entries sharing the id. curr-334 already satisfies this and should be cited in SKILL.md as the pattern to copy.
improvements.regression_test: New fixture from curr-301 problem 4: a stem enumerating (a) write the converse, (b) compute QR, (c) explain why PQRS makes the converse false, paired with the single verify entry {"id": 4, "type": "distance", "expected": 3}. The lint must fail with 'problem 4: 3 printed slots, 1 verify entry'. The current tree passes this fixture - it is what shipped.
improvements.expected_impact: Closes the largest verification blind spot in the shard: sheets that read as fully verified while a third of what the student writes is unrecorded, and answer keys whose Quick Answers bank prints one value for a two-answer question.
improvements.risk: Low-medium. The \item count is a heuristic: a sub-part that is pure scaffolding ('redraw the two triangles separately first') is not a response slot and would false-positive. Let the author mark such an item so the exclusion is auditable rather than silent.

case_summary: An excellent counterexample-and-precise-definition packet. All six machine items and both manual model answers are mathematically correct on independent recomputation, the coordinate-test framing is the right pedagogical choice for this focus, and the study guide's three sections (definition to coordinate test, kill a claim with one counterexample, repair a loose definition) each carry a rule, a worked example and a verified try-it. Two defects the judge did not reach: the sheet is tagged HSG-GPE.B.4-B.7 instead of the contracted HSG-CO, justified by a false claim that the code is absent from references/standards-map.md (it is at line 111); and problems 1-5 each print a required written explanation - problem 4 prints three enumerated slots - with no verify entry, machine or manual, covering it. Neither changes the ACCEPT verdict; both are systemic and recur across this shard.
